  La Paz is the capital of Baja California Sur, Mexico, on the Gulf of California. Visitors come for the Malecón waterfront, Balandra and Tecolote beaches, boat trips to Espíritu Santo Island and the gulf's marine wildlife. Planning should take account of protected-area rules, sea conditions and the seasons for water excursions.
---

## La Paz, Mexico: the Gulf of California, beaches and boat trips

**La Paz is located in Baja California Sur on the Gulf of California.** Unlike Mexico's larger resort centres, the city makes it easy to combine waterfront walks, local food and excursions into protected marine areas.

Do not confuse this Mexican La Paz with the city of the same name in Bolivia. The Mexican destination lies on the Baja California Peninsula, and its principal attractions are associated with the Sea of Cortez, the coastal desert, islands and marine wildlife.

## The Malecón waterfront and walking around town

The **Malecón** promenade is a convenient place to begin exploring La Paz. Walkways stretch along the water, with sculptures, cafés and restaurants. You can watch fishing boats and sunsets over the gulf before continuing into the central neighbourhoods.

The city's older quarters contain a cathedral and historic buildings connected to its development as a port. A walk around town reveals La Paz as a state capital, rather than simply a departure point for beach trips.

For an evening stroll along the Malecón, allow some free time after your marine excursion. Boat-trip durations and return times depend on weather, so squeezing several water activities into a tightly scheduled day is often impractical.

## Balandra Beach: turquoise shallows and conservation rules

**Balandra** is one of the best-known beaches near La Paz. Its shallow coves are enclosed by dry hills, and the pale sand contrasts strikingly with the turquoise water. The local tourism portal identifies it as a protected natural area.

Balandra is known for a mushroom-shaped rock. More importantly, it is a conservation site with limits on visitor numbers and rules governing access. The municipal authorities describe visiting shifts, capacity restrictions and special permit procedures. Arrangements can change, so check the current CONANP access rules before travelling.

| Place | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Balandra | Shallow water and coves |
| El Tecolote | Beach relaxation |
| Malecón | City life and sunsets |
| Espíritu Santo | Islands and marine life |

At Balandra, follow protected-area rules, take your rubbish away and avoid disturbing mangroves or the wildlife of coastal ecosystems. Swimming and other water activities depend on which sections are open.

## Espíritu Santo Island and marine excursions

**Espíritu Santo** is a protected island area in the Gulf of California. Boat trips from La Paz offer views of rocky coves, desert island landscapes and, under suitable conditions, marine animals.

The local tourism authority notes that the island belongs to the protected-area system, so visitors must follow its regulations and use authorised operators. A boat excursion may involve cruising, stops at beaches or snorkelling, but the precise itinerary depends on permits, sea conditions and the excursion package.

Swimming near sea lions and observing them are governed by additional conservation requirements. Such experiences may appear in general visitor descriptions of the island, but they are not guaranteed on every date or programme.

## Whale sharks and other marine wildlife

One of the gulf's best-known wildlife experiences is **whale shark watching**. These large fish can appear in waters near La Paz. City authorities describe a specially protected area and a visiting season, but the actual opening of tours depends on conservation decisions and the presence of animals.

Whale shark encounters are subject to limits on vessel numbers, distances and people's behaviour in the water. Swimming, where permitted, takes place under the rules of authorised operators. A sighting on a particular day, or even permission to enter the water, cannot be guaranteed in advance.

The gulf is also home to other marine species. A boat excursion does not necessarily mean that participants will see dolphins, rays or rare fish. For a wildlife-focused journey, it is worth allowing several days so that an outing can be selected according to weather conditions.

## Sport fishing, diving and beach holidays

La Paz has long been a destination for **sport fishing**. Specific seasons, permitted species, catch limits and handling rules must be checked against local requirements. The skipper's qualifications, vessel safety and the actual plan for the day are important.

Scuba diving and snorkelling in the Gulf of California are also standalone activities. When planning them, consider participants' experience, available equipment, certifications and intended dive sites. If the sea is your main interest, explore [fishing tours](/interests/fishing/) and [diving](/interests/diving/).

Travellers who prefer relaxing on land should allow a separate beach day. Balandra's restricted access and more flexible beach stays elsewhere are different experiences. A beautiful sea view does not necessarily mean that a particular stretch of shore is safe for swimming in any weather.

## Planning a journey to La Paz

For a first visit, a city walk, one beach day and a separate boat excursion make a practical combination. If Espíritu Santo or whale shark watching is your main goal, choose dates around the permitted season and allow for possible rescheduling.

Travel logistics differ from mainland Mexico. La Paz can be linked with other destinations on the Baja California Peninsula, such as [Cabo San Lucas](/mexico/place/cabo-san-lucas/), but that requires separate road transfers and additional days.

We can help design a customised itinerary in [Mexico](/mexico/), with beaches, marine nature and cities spread across the days. Excursions and transfers depend on the chosen programme and are not determined simply by staying in La Paz.

## Frequently asked questions about La Paz

### Where is La Paz in Mexico?

It is in Baja California Sur on the Gulf of California. It is a different city from La Paz in Bolivia.

### Can I visit Balandra without restrictions?

No. Balandra is a protected natural area with regulated access. Check the current arrangements before visiting.

### Is it possible to see whale sharks?

Tours operate during certain periods and subject to official permission. Encounters depend on natural conditions and current conservation restrictions.

### How many days should I allow for La Paz?

For a first visit, it is sensible to spend separate days exploring town, enjoying a beach and taking a marine excursion, with some flexibility for poor weather.

## Mérida: attractions in the capital of Yucatán

Mérida lies on Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula. Its historic centre offers colonial buildings, leafy squares and everyday city life. It is a convenient destination for travellers interested in both ancient Maya monuments and Yucatecan cuisine.

From Mérida, you can visit [Uxmal](/mexico/place/uxmal/), [Chichén Itzá](/mexico/place/chichen-itza/) and natural cenotes. The city itself also deserves time: evening streets, museums and markets provide experiences that archaeological sites cannot.

This is **Mérida in Mexico**. Another city of the same name exists in Venezuela; the two should not be confused when planning a Yucatán itinerary or choosing transport.

## Plaza Grande and the cathedral

**Plaza Grande**, the main square, is the natural starting point for discovering Mérida. Here you will find the Cathedral of San Ildefonso, Casa de Montejo and historic government buildings. Within a small area, visitors can see different architectural periods and learn about colonial Mérida.

**The cathedral** was built during the sixteenth century and remains the principal landmark of the central neighbourhoods. **Casa de Montejo** recalls the early decades of the Spanish city and is now associated with museums and cultural activities. Nearby streets are ideal for leisurely walks between shops and cafés.

When exploring the centre, it is more rewarding to choose a few buildings and a museum than to rush through every attraction on a short stop. On hot days, plan much of the walk for morning or evening.

## Paseo de Montejo and historic neighbourhoods

**Paseo de Montejo** is a broad avenue lined with historic mansions and monumental façades. It reflects Yucatán's economic prosperity during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. The district looks very different from the denser colonial streets around Plaza Grande and is worth a separate walk.

**Santa Ana**, **Santa Lucía** and **Santiago** are neighbourhoods known for their squares, restaurants and local markets. Cultural performances take place in some locations, although schedules vary by weekday. For an evening out, choose an event actually taking place rather than assuming entertainment is offered every night.

To enjoy Mérida's atmosphere, begin in the centre during the day, then walk along Paseo de Montejo towards evening and explore a nearby neighbourhood. Transport is mainly needed to reach more distant sites.

## Yucatecan food: what to try

Mérida is a good place to sample regional dishes such as **cochinita pibil**, **panuchos**, **salbutes**, corn tortillas and a range of sauces. Yucatecan cuisine uses local spices and vegetables and traditional meat-cooking methods. Check the ingredients of particular dishes if you have allergies or dietary restrictions.

Markets such as **Lucas de Gálvez**, **Santa Ana** and **Santiago** offer local produce and freshly prepared food. They are a good way to experience ordinary city life, especially after days devoted mostly to museums and archaeological monuments.

The centre has both traditional and contemporary restaurants. When choosing a [food-focused journey](/interests/food-and-wine/), check whether specific tastings or cooking classes are included. An ordinary restaurant lunch and a complete gastronomic programme offer very different experiences.

## Uxmal and Kabah: Maya monuments near Mérida

[Uxmal](/mexico/place/uxmal/) is one of the best-known Maya archaeological complexes, associated with the Puuc architectural style. Its major monuments include the Pyramid of the Magician and buildings with rich stone ornamentation. Allow time for the journey and for exploring the outdoor site.

[Kabah](/mexico/place/kabah/) lies in the same historic region and is often paired with Uxmal on itineraries. Seeing both sites helps illustrate how Puuc architecture differs from monuments elsewhere in Mesoamerica.

A more distant excursion destination is [Chichén Itzá](/mexico/place/chichen-itza/). Longer itineraries may continue onwards after Mérida rather than return to the same hotel. Compare the actual day-by-day sequence and transfers when choosing a programme.

## Cenotes and natural experiences

The Yucatán Peninsula is rich in cenotes, natural waterbodies in limestone formations. They vary in depth, open-water access, lighting, requirements to wear life jackets and swimming arrangements.

Our Yucatán itineraries can include the [Santa Bárbara cenotes](/mexico/place/santa-barbara-cenotes/). They make a separate nature-focused day, distinct from exploring archaeological cities. Check the rules for swimming and transport in the specific programme.

Mérida lies inland, not on the coast. If beaches are your priority, you will need a separate transfer to the seaside or a coastal stay added to the urban part of your journey.

## Mérida on Ada Tours itineraries

The [12-day Viva Mexico: Mexico City, Oaxaca and Yucatán](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/) links several cultural regions. After the capital and Oaxaca, the itinerary includes Mérida, Uxmal, cenotes and other Yucatán sites.

On [Mexico Lindo: 8 Days from Mexico City to the Caribbean Coast](/mexico/tour/mexico-lindo-eight-days/), you spend **3 nights in Mérida** and visit Uxmal, Kabah, the Santa Bárbara cenotes and Chichén Itzá. Under this programme's terms, the domestic Mexico City–Mérida flight is paid separately. Such details matter when comparing costs and logistics.

There is also a shorter [Mexico City–Mérida–Uxmal and Kabah–Chichén Itzá itinerary](/mexico/tour/mexico-city-merida-uxmal-kabah-chichen-itza/). To choose the right format, compare overnight stays, excursions and interregional transfers in the [Mexico tours catalogue](/mexico/tour/).

## When to visit and how much time to allow

Mérida is often hot. Morning and evening are generally more comfortable for walking through the historic centre; midday can be reserved for a museum and a rest. Heavy rain sometimes affects roads and excursions, so it is useful to allow flexibility for archaeological visits.

One day is enough for the main central neighbourhoods. If you also plan to see Uxmal and the cenotes, **2–4 nights** is more sensible, with excursions distributed across the stay. Visiting a historical site and swimming in a cenote require different preparations and amounts of time.

## Frequently asked questions about Mérida

### Is Mérida by the sea?

No. Mérida is an inland city on the Yucatán Peninsula. Visitors choose it for architecture, cuisine and excursions; a beach day requires separate transport.

### What should I see on my first day?

Start at Plaza Grande, the cathedral and Casa de Montejo. Then walk along Paseo de Montejo and choose one of the old neighbourhoods for dinner.

### Can I visit Uxmal from Mérida?

Yes. [Uxmal](/mexico/place/uxmal/) is one of the principal archaeological excursions from the city and requires a substantial part of the day.

### Are there organised tours with overnight stays in Mérida?

Yes. For instance, [Mexico Lindo: 8 Days](/mexico/tour/mexico-lindo-eight-days/) includes 3 nights in the city and excursions across Yucatán.

## Which tours through Mérida can you choose?

[Mérida](/mexico/place/merida/) in Mexico's Yucatán state forms part of the main itinerary on several current Ada Tours programmes. Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The main differences are **how many nights are spent in the city, how much sightseeing is provided and how travellers reach Yucatán**. This page concerns Mérida in Mexico, not the city of the same name in Venezuela.

For an initial comparison, consider five different formats:

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_bolshie_meksikanskie_kanikuly,tour_source_viva_meksika,tour_source_meksika_lindo,tour_mexico_lindo_eight_days,tour_central_america_eight_countries_26_days}}

The [Grand Mexico Holiday](/mexico/tour/grand-mexico-holiday/) lasts 6 days. The route passes through Mexico City, Palenque, Campeche and Uxmal, reaches Mérida, then continues to Chichén Itzá and the Caribbean coast. The emphasis is on a sequence of archaeological sites and transfers.

[Viva Mexico](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/) lasts 12 days and combines Mexico City, Oaxaca and Yucatán. On day 9, the Mérida programme includes arrival by air and a walk through the historic centre. [Mexico Lindo: 8 Days](/mexico/tour/mexico-lindo-eight-days/) includes **3 nights in Mérida**, making it a base for excursions to Uxmal, Kabah, cenotes and Chichén Itzá.

The six-day [Mexico City–Mérida–Uxmal and Kabah–Chichén Itzá tour](/mexico/tour/mexico-city-merida-uxmal-kabah-chichen-itza/) is especially interesting for travellers who want to combine museums in the capital with Maya archaeology. Arrival time in Mérida is particularly important: to preserve the scheduled day 4 excursion, the flight must arrive **before 13:00**, and the domestic ticket is paid separately.

Finally, Mérida appears near the start of the [26-day journey through eight Central American countries](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/). Here the visit needs to be considered alongside the other countries and long transfers, not as a standalone holiday in Yucatán.

## Mérida as a sightseeing stop and as a base for excursions

These two ways of visiting Mérida create different experiences.

**A short stop with city sightseeing.** Travellers see the Cathedral of San Ildefonso, the main square and historic façades, sometimes including Paseo de Montejo. [Viva Mexico](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/) schedules a city walk lasting approximately 2.5–3 hours. On the six-day [Mexico City–Mérida tour](/mexico/tour/mexico-city-merida-uxmal-kabah-chichen-itza/), the sightseeing walk lasts around 2 hours.

**Several nights with excursions from the city.** On the eight-day [Mexico Lindo](/mexico/tour/mexico-lindo-eight-days/), Mérida is the base for visits to [Uxmal](/mexico/place/uxmal/), [Kabah](/mexico/place/kabah/) and the [Santa Bárbara cenotes](/mexico/place/santa-barbara-cenotes/). This reduces the need for constant hotel changes and makes excursions across central Yucatán easier.

When choosing, check **whether a guided tour of Mérida itself is actually scheduled**. An overnight stay does not automatically include a guided walk through the centre or its museums. On the [Grand Mexico Holiday](/mexico/tour/grand-mexico-holiday/), for instance, the itinerary describes the transfer after Uxmal and accommodation in a Mérida hotel, while the following day is dedicated to Chichén Itzá and the journey onwards to the coast.

## Which Yucatán attractions are commonly combined with Mérida?

Mérida is a convenient departure point for different historical and archaeological routes. To understand ancient Maya architecture, visit several sites: their layouts, decoration and historical roles differ.

| Place | What it adds to the trip |
|---|---|
| [Mérida](/mexico/place/merida/) | Colonial centre and city life |
| [Uxmal](/mexico/place/uxmal/) | Puuc-region architecture |
| [Kabah](/mexico/place/kabah/) | Elaborate Maya temple reliefs |
| [Chichén Itzá](/mexico/place/chichen-itza/) | A monumental ancient city |
| [Santa Bárbara cenotes](/mexico/place/santa-barbara-cenotes/) | Swimming in natural pools |

[Uxmal](/mexico/place/uxmal/) lies south of Mérida. Its famous buildings include the Pyramid of the Magician and the Governor's Palace. [Kabah](/mexico/place/kabah/) belongs to the same Puuc cultural and historical region but is particularly known for its richly decorated façades, including depictions of the rain god Chaac. Excursions to these monuments reveal differences within the Maya architectural tradition.

[Chichén Itzá](/mexico/place/chichen-itza/) often comes **after Mérida** on journeys towards Cancún or the Riviera Maya. Several Ada Tours itineraries follow this order. Visits to the [cenotes](/mexico/place/santa-barbara-cenotes/) provide a change of experience, replacing city streets and stone temples with natural limestone pools. Swimming, admission fees and guiding are included only where explicitly stated in the programme.

There is also time in Mérida to discover local food. Yucatán is known for cochinita pibil, sopa de lima and papadzules. A suggestion to try these in your free time does not mean that a gastronomic excursion or a particular restaurant is included in the paid tour.

## How itineraries differ in length

| Format | Main difference |
|---|---|
| 6 days | A busy route through Maya monuments |
| 8 days | Several nights and excursions from Mérida |
| 12 days | Mexico City, Oaxaca and Yucatán |
| 26 days | Eight Central American countries |

**Six-day programmes** are best for travellers who want to connect Yucatán with Mexico City or Chiapas in limited time. On the [Cancún–Tulum–Palenque–Uxmal–Chichén Itzá itinerary](/mexico/tour/mexico-cancun-tulum-palenque-uxmal-chichen-itza/), day 5 includes a transfer from Uxmal to Mérida, a sightseeing tour and a stay in a 4-star hotel.

**The eight-day programme** is more convenient for travellers who want Mérida as a base for several excursions. **The 12-day Viva Mexico** spends more time in other regions too, so judging it only by its Yucatán days would be misleading.

**The 26-day itinerary** belongs to a different category of travel. After Mexico, it continues through Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama. Choose it for the full regional experience, not to increase the time spent in one city.

## Flights, transfers and inclusions: what to check

**Domestic flights and sightseeing services must be compared separately for every tour.** On the six-day [Mexico City–Mérida programme](/mexico/tour/mexico-city-merida-uxmal-kabah-chichen-itza/), the flight from the capital is paid separately and arrival before 13:00 is essential for keeping the itinerary. On [Mexico Lindo: 8 Days](/mexico/tour/mexico-lindo-eight-days/), the domestic flight is also excluded, although airport transfers and a city walk are specified.

On [Viva Mexico](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/), day 9 links Oaxaca and Mérida by air, with the ticket explicitly marked as excluded in that day's description. A city sightseeing tour is planned on arrival day, so the flight schedule affects whether travellers can join the walk.

**Guides and transfers vary.** Some days provide private services, while others use group transport and bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking guides. The eight-day itinerary, for example, includes a private transfer upon arrival in Mérida and a group excursion to Uxmal and Kabah. Do not assume the arrangements on one day apply to the whole tour.

Compare not only the headline price, but also accommodation, domestic flights, admission fees, meals and potential additional expenses. Each tour's terms are given in its [individual programme](/mexico/tour/).

## Planning around the weather

Yucatán has a warm climate and many city walks and archaeological sites offer little shade. Drinking water and sun protection are important in the historic centre, while comfortable shoes are useful for archaeological excursions. In the rainy season, allow extra time for road transfers and possible downpours.

If cenotes are on your itinerary, pack swimming items separately from clothing for museums and temples. A multi-day trip across Mexico's different regions calls for clothes suitable for both higher-altitude cities and hot Yucatán.

Check current opening hours and local restrictions at archaeological sites, as these can change. Excursion times also depend on transfers and weather. Other travel formats are available in the [Mexico tours catalogue](/mexico/tour/), and the city itself is described on our [Mérida page](/mexico/place/merida/).

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting Mérida

### Is there a tour in this selection with several nights in Mérida?

Yes. [Mexico Lindo: 8 Days](/mexico/tour/mexico-lindo-eight-days/) includes **3 nights in Mérida** and excursions to Uxmal, Kabah, cenotes and Chichén Itzá.

### Can I visit Mérida without a separate domestic flight?

On some itineraries, Mérida is reached by road after Campeche and Uxmal. Others include a flight from Mexico City or Oaxaca. The choice depends on the entire route, not on a single destination.

### Which tours devote more attention to the city rather than archaeological sites?

[Viva Mexico](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/) describes a guided walk through the historic centre after arrival. The [six-day Mexico City–Mérida itinerary](/mexico/tour/mexico-city-merida-uxmal-kabah-chichen-itza/) also includes a sightseeing walk past the central landmarks.

### Are Mérida and Uxmal included in the same itinerary?

Yes, on several current programmes. However, the dates and order differ: sometimes Uxmal is visited **before** checking into a hotel in Mérida, and sometimes travellers go **from Mérida** on a separate excursion day.

### Are all admission tickets and domestic flights included?

There is no single rule for the entire catalogue. Domestic flights, for instance, are excluded from the base price on some of the programmes listed here. Admission-ticket inclusions depend on the specific excursions. Check the details on your chosen tour page.

## Mexico City and Teotihuacan: combining the capital with the pyramids

**[Mexico City](/mexico/) is the country's capital, while [Teotihuacan](/mexico/place/teotihuacan/) is an ancient archaeological site outside the city.** They are often combined on a single sightseeing tour, but their histories are distinct. In the capital's centre, travellers discover the Aztec city of Tenochtitlan, colonial architecture and museums. At Teotihuacan, they see the layout of a much older city.

This page brings Mexico City and the ruins of Teotihuacan together as one sightseeing route. Geographically, the pyramids are in the State of Mexico, northeast of the capital, not inside its historic centre. Allow separate travel time to reach them.

## Mexico City's historic centre: where to begin

A first walk can begin around **[Zócalo Square](/mexico/place/mexico-city-zocalo/)**. Nearby are the Metropolitan Cathedral, government buildings and remains of ancient Tenochtitlan. Within this area, you can trace the city's evolution from the pre-Columbian period to the modern capital.

**[Templo Mayor](/mexico/place/templo-mayor/)** was part of the Aztec capital's religious centre. After the Spanish conquest, a city of New Spain rose on the site of Tenochtitlan. A single walk therefore brings archaeological remains, colonial buildings and present-day streets together.

Mexico City's historic centre, along with Xochimilco, is on the UNESCO World Heritage List. This is a separate UNESCO property from ancient Teotihuacan: they belong to different historical periods and have different boundaries and monuments.

## Mexico City museums and the heritage of ancient civilisations

**The National Museum of Anthropology** helps visitors understand Mesoamerican cultures before heading to the pyramids. Its exhibitions feature material from different civilisations, including the Aztecs and the people of Teotihuacan. A museum visit is valuable if you want to understand what you see beyond simply knowing the names of the pyramids.

The museum is in the [Chapultepec](/mexico/place/chapultepec/) area, with a large park and other cultural attractions. On a short visit to Mexico City, you could reserve a separate half-day for the museum and park rather than trying to combine them mechanically with every monument around Zócalo.

Travellers interested in art and colonial history may also enjoy the National Palace, known for its murals by Diego Rivera, and other historic central buildings. Access to government buildings should be checked for your particular date; a landmark appearing on a map does not mean it is always open.

## Teotihuacan: Pyramid of the Sun, Pyramid of the Moon and Avenue of the Dead

**[Teotihuacan](/mexico/place/teotihuacan/)** is a pre-Columbian Mesoamerican site added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1987. According to Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH), the archaeological area open to visitors covers approximately 264 hectares. Its major structures are connected by the **Avenue of the Dead**.

The site includes the Pyramid of the Sun, the Pyramid of the Moon, the Ciudadela complex and the Temple of the Feathered Serpent. Fragments of murals and residential compounds survive, offering insight into both religious ceremonies and everyday life in the great city.

Teotihuacan existed long before the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan reached its height. Its pyramids should therefore not be described as Aztec constructions: the Aztecs knew the abandoned ancient city and regarded it as sacred, but founded their own capital in a different historical era.

## How much time should you allow for the pyramids?

The archaeological zone is large and exposed. Exploring the major structures takes several hours on foot, often in direct sunlight along stone paths and open spaces. It is better to prioritise selected areas than to rush through every complex without stopping.

| Place | What to see |
|---|---|
| Pyramid of the Sun | Monumental architecture |
| Pyramid of the Moon | Northern part of the complex |
| Avenue of the Dead | Ancient city layout |
| Temple of Quetzalcoatl | Reliefs and ancient worship |

Additional on-site museums cover material culture and wall paintings. Visiting them requires extra time. INAH sets opening hours and rules for access to the monuments, so do not assume that climbing the pyramids or entering every restricted area is permitted on any given day.

Bring water, a hat, sunscreen and comfortable shoes for extended walking. In hot weather, plan most of the visit before the strongest midday sun.

## Getting to Teotihuacan from Mexico City

The archaeological complex lies northeast of the capital. Driving time depends on traffic and your departure point, so an excursion outside the city needs a realistic transport allowance. After arriving, you will also need time to walk from the entrance to your chosen structures.

Some sightseeing programmes combine Teotihuacan with the [Basilica of Guadalupe](/mexico/place/basilica-of-guadalupe/). This makes sense thematically, but each site has its own visitor rules and takes time to explore. Start planning with the hours actually available, rather than the longest possible list of attractions.

If you have only one sightseeing day in Mexico City, it is sensible to choose a priority: exploring the historic centre and museums in depth, or making a separate trip to the pyramids. To do both comfortably, allow more time.

## Mexico City and Teotihuacan on Ada Tours itineraries

On [Mexico Lindo: 8 Days from Mexico City to the Caribbean Coast](/mexico/tour/mexico-lindo-eight-days/), your introduction to the country begins in the capital before the journey continues. On the [26-day tour of Central America](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/), Mexico City and Teotihuacan feature in the early days, before you travel onwards through Mexico and neighbouring countries.

The best choice depends on the overall duration, the number of days spent in the capital and time for archaeology. For a journey dedicated to Mexico, see [Mexico tours](/mexico/tour/) and [cultural and historical itineraries](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about Mexico City and Teotihuacan

### Is Teotihuacan in Mexico City?

No. It is a separate archaeological complex northeast of the capital, reached by car or bus.

### Did the Aztecs build the pyramids of Teotihuacan?

No. The city existed long before the rise of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan. The Aztecs later knew it as a sacred place.

### Can you see the pyramids in one day?

Yes. Day trips are regularly organised from Mexico City; allow several hours for the archaeological site itself.

### What should I see in central Mexico City before visiting the pyramids?

[Zócalo](/mexico/place/mexico-city-zocalo/), [Templo Mayor](/mexico/place/templo-mayor/) and the National Museum of Anthropology make a useful introduction to the region's history.

## Which tours visit Mexico City and Teotihuacan?

Mexico City is the starting point for many sightseeing itineraries across Mexico. Here you will find **{{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}** that include [Mexico City and the Teotihuacan area](/mexico/place/mexico-city-and-teotihuacan/) as a principal stop. This is a useful starting point for choosing a journey, but the tours differ in their subsequent geography, excursions and duration.

In the capital, you can see [Zócalo Square](/mexico/place/mexico-city-zocalo/), the [Metropolitan Cathedral](/mexico/place/mexico-city-metropolitan-cathedral/), [Templo Mayor](/mexico/place/templo-mayor/) and the [National Museum of Anthropology](/mexico/place/national-museum-of-anthropology/). Outside the city is the separate archaeological complex of [Teotihuacan](/mexico/place/teotihuacan/), approximately 50 km northeast of the capital. Its surviving monuments include the Pyramid of the Sun, Pyramid of the Moon, Avenue of the Dead and Temple of the Feathered Serpent.

An important distinction when choosing: the words 'Mexico City' on an itinerary confirm that the capital is included. If you want to explore the pyramids, look for a dedicated Teotihuacan day or an explicit reference to that excursion on the selected tour.

## Four different travel formats

**[Mexico Lindo: 8 Days](/mexico/tour/mexico-lindo-eight-days/)** suits travellers who want to explore the capital before continuing to Yucatán. The next stage takes in [Mérida](/mexico/place/merida/), [Uxmal](/mexico/place/uxmal/), cenotes and [Chichén Itzá](/mexico/place/chichen-itza/). After Mexico City and Teotihuacan, the itinerary explores [Oaxaca](/mexico/place/oaxaca/), craft workshops, [Monte Albán](/mexico/place/monte-alban/) and ancient cities of Yucatán. ## Historic centre and pyramids: how much time to allow

For a meaningful introduction to the capital, it is sensible to allow at least a full day for its historic core. [Zócalo](/mexico/place/mexico-city-zocalo/) is surrounded by colonial buildings, while [Templo Mayor](/mexico/place/templo-mayor/) recalls the city of Tenochtitlan that stood here before the Spanish conquest. The anthropology museum and [Chapultepec Park](/mexico/place/chapultepec/) are in another district. Trying to see all these places in a few hours turns the visit into a string of brief stops.

Allow a separate part of a day for the [Teotihuacan archaeological zone](/mexico/place/teotihuacan/), including the drive from Mexico City. According to Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History, the visitor area contains several large complexes and museums. Exploring it requires extensive walking across an open site; water, a hat and comfortable footwear are essential in sunny weather. Check current opening hours and access arrangements for individual structures before travelling.

UNESCO lists the ancient city of Teotihuacan as a World Heritage site in its own right. Mexico City's historic centre is also listed, but as part of a different property, together with Xochimilco. They represent distinct chapters of the region's cultural history, each deserving its own time.

## What to check before choosing a tour

Begin with your arrival day and the number of nights in the capital. If an itinerary allows only one night in Mexico City, it is difficult to combine a proper museum visit, a walk through the historic centre and an excursion to the pyramids. Check which visits are compulsory and which are offered as optional extras.

Next, consider where the journey continues. For archaeology and colonial history, itineraries including [Oaxaca](/mexico/place/oaxaca/) and Yucatán work well. For religious history, look for programmes with the [Basilica of Guadalupe](/mexico/place/basilica-of-guadalupe/) and churches in the central states. On an extended journey across several borders, separately consider flights, transfers, travel documents and time to rest between journeys.

Compare the included excursions, guiding language, tickets and transport on each specific tour. The same city can feature in both private and group programmes, and shared geography does not imply identical arrangements. If your main priority is a one-day excursion to the pyramids, consider the [Teotihuacan and Shrine of Guadalupe excursion](/mexico/teotihuacan/teotihuacan-guadalupe-tour/) rather than choosing a multi-day itinerary for just one attraction.

## Questions about itineraries through Mexico City

### Do all the tours in this selection include Teotihuacan?

No. The selection covers itineraries through the combined Mexico City and surrounding region. A visit to the actual pyramids is confirmed only by the relevant day or excursion in a given itinerary. Mexico Lindo and Viva Mexico both list a separate excursion there.

### How many days should I stay in Mexico City?

To explore the historic centre and dedicate a day to Teotihuacan, plan several days in the capital. Museums, Xochimilco and other districts will require additional time. The precise duration depends on the excursions and transport arrangements.

### Can I combine Teotihuacan with Yucatán?

Yes. For example, [the eight-day Mexico Lindo](/mexico/tour/mexico-lindo-eight-days/) combines the capital and Teotihuacan with Mérida, Uxmal, Chichén Itzá and the Caribbean coast. Remember that the domestic flight is paid separately.

### Is a pilgrimage tour suitable for ordinary city sightseeing?

It does include architecture and historic landmarks, but much of its programme centres on shrines and 5 Masses. If your interests are mainly secular, compare [cultural and historical tours of Mexico](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/mexico/) and other options.

### How does this selection differ from all tours of Mexico?

Here you will find itineraries that actually pass through Mexico City and its associated route area. The [general Mexico tours catalogue](/mexico/tour/) also includes journeys beginning in Yucatán, on the Caribbean coast and in other parts of the country.
